recommendation.evidence_assessment: Moderate confidence. Canonical guidance (MISEV2023) and recent rodent/NHP studies consistently indicate the need for orthogonal characterization, MCB/WCB, validated potency/stability assays, and controlled bridging studies. However, the program-provided package lacks program-specific assay validation, numeric acceptance criteria, and scaled-run data; conclusions therefore depend on established guidance and precautionary interpretation of cross-species literature rather than internal validated experimental results.
findings: Program lacks validated, orthogonal intact-EV analytics, a characterized source cell bank (MCB/WCB), and multi-batch scale-up/stability data necessary to de-risk claims that a specific intranasal formulation preserves EV identity or yields reproducible intact-EV CNS exposure.

MISEV2023 consensus and available rodent/NHP biodistribution literature support a CMC/analytics gate before advancing formulation-focused delivery testing; rodent intranasal results do not reliably predict intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species without orthogonal intact-EV assays and bridging controls.

Advancing a formulation into higher-confidence device/delivery and cross-species biodistribution testing before completing a defined Stage 1 CMC/analytics package would risk generating misleading attribution of signal (intact EV vs non-vesicular artefact) and wasting in vivo resources.
objections: Do not advance a specific intranasal formulation into higher-confidence delivery testing yet because the program lacks validated, orthogonal analytics, MCB/WCB and demonstrated process reproducibility/stability, and any intact-EV CNS exposure across species — without those CMC and assay de-risks, formulation compatibility and in vivo bridging studies cannot reliably assess intact-EV delivery or mechanism.

claim_updates.rationale: No MCB/WCB, validated scale-up or reproducibility data provided; MISEV recommends defined production controls and reporting.
claim_updates.statement: Current materials do not demonstrate characterized source-cell MCB/WCB or scalable, reproducible production sufficient to support advancing a specific intranasal formulation.

claim_updates.rationale: MISEV2023 consensus supports orthogonal characterization and transparent release/assay criteria to de-risk identity and potency claims.
claim_updates.statement: An orthogonal QC panel (particles, protein, lipid markers per MISEV), validated intact-EV assays (LLOQ, specificity, precision), and stability-indicating, mechanism-linked potency assays are required before formulation advancement.

claim_updates.rationale: Cross-species biodistribution literature and characterization guidance indicate limited translatability absent orthogonal intact-EV analytics and controlled bridging studies.
claim_updates.statement: Rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone are insufficient to predict reproducible intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species without matching intact-EV assays and bridging controls.

decision_update.question: Should a specific intranasal formulation be advanced into controlled compatibility and delivery testing for SGL-001?
decision_update.rationale: Recommend completing Stage 1 CMC/analytics/formulation-compatibility gate before advancing to Stage 2 biodistribution/bridging. Advancement to Stage 2 requires human approval after Stage 1 acceptance criteria are met.

proposed_changes.editorial_clarification: When referring to 'large species,' clarify that species selection should be data-driven; NHP is an option but not mandated by the current evidence.

hypothesis_update.rationale: To ensure observed in vivo signal is attributable to intact EV and is reproducible across lots/species, the program must meet orthogonal analytical and process reproducibility criteria before bridging studies.
hypothesis_update.statement: Advancing an intranasal formulation into high-confidence delivery and cross-species PK/PD testing requires completion of a defined CMC/analytics/formulation compatibility gating package.
hypothesis_update.test_plan: Stage 1 completion criteria: MCB/WCB produced; orthogonal QC panel defined and assays fit-for-purpose validated (LLOQ, specificity, precision); stability-indicating potency assay correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint; reproducible release/stability/potency across ≥3 GMP-like batches; formulation/device compatibility with intact-EV recovery demonstrated ex vivo and in vivo (controls included).

proposed_changes.next_action: Implement Stage 1 with timebound subprojects: source-cell/MCB-WCB (timeline + owner), orthogonal QC panel + draft release specs, fit-for-purpose validation of potency/stability assays, three representative GMP-like scale-up runs with release/stability assessment, and formulation/device compatibility testing with ex vivo nasal model and in vivo rodent tests including disrupted-EV and free-label controls.

risk_updates.description: Lack of MCB/WCB, orthogonal QC, validated potency/stability assays, and scale-up reproducibility may produce misleading in vitro and in vivo results and block regulatory acceptance.
risk_updates.mitigation: Execute Stage 1 actions: generate MCB/WCB, define/validate orthogonal assays, produce representative GMP-like batches, and document stability/potency reproducibility. Escalate assay development resourcing if timelines slip.
risk_updates.title: Insufficient CMC/analytics to establish intact-EV identity, potency, and lot-to-lot reproducibility

risk_updates.description: Rodent intranasal biodistribution may not predict large-species/NHP CNS exposure for intact EV; device and formulation interactions may differ by species.
risk_updates.mitigation: Require ex vivo nasal recovery and rodent intact-EV-specific PK with controls prior to any large-species study; predefine bridging acceptance criteria and include disrupted-EV and free-label controls in all in vivo studies.
risk_updates.title: Cross-species translation uncertainty for intranasal intact-EV CNS exposure

recommendation.recommendation: Execute a timebound Stage 1 gate (CMC + analytics + formulation compatibility) prior to advancing any intranasal formulation into controlled delivery or cross-species biodistribution testing. Stage 1 priorities: (1) finalize source-cell selection and create MCB/WCB; (2) define an orthogonal QC panel per MISEV and draft release specifications; (3) develop/qualify stability-indicating and mechanism-linked potency assays to at least fit-for-purpose; (4) produce ≥3 representative GMP-like scale-up batches to demonstrate release assay reproducibility, potency, and stability; (5) perform formulation/device compatibility testing measuring intact-EV recovery and identity (include disrupted-EV and free-label controls). Do not proceed to Stage 2 biodistribution/PK/PD bridging until predefined analytical acceptance criteria are met. Any decision to advance to Stage 2 requires human approval and remains pending.
